summary: A municipal reporting API allowing citizens to submit reports with photos, track status via notifications, and interact via internal comments or public messages. It supports role-based workflows for review (admin), assignment (technical office), and external maintenance (external maintainers). Includes user management, session handling, Telegram integration, and street search.

authentication_notes: Most endpoints require authentication via session tokens obtained from /sessions.
Anonymous report creation (/reports/anonymous) does not require authentication.
Telegram webhook endpoint is publicly accessible without auth.
User registration and confirmation flow requires email verification before full access.
Operations marked auth_required need an authenticated session during test setup.
dependencies: POST /sessions must precede any authenticated request requiring user identity.
POST /users creates a citizen account; POST /users/confirm finalizes registration.
GET /api/categories is a prerequisite for creating reports (both authenticated and anonymous).
PUT /reports/{id}/review depends on the report being in 'pending' state (accessible via GET /reports/pending).
PUT /reports/{id}/assign-external requires the report to be in 'assigned' status (accessible via GET /reports/assigned).
PUT /reports/{id}/status is only valid for reports assigned to external maintainers.
GET /streets enables autocomplete; GET /streets/{name}/reports depends on a valid street name from the search.
POST /users/admin and POST /users/{id}/assign-role require admin privileges established via prior auth.
GET /users/roles is only meaningful after admin context is set (via /sessions or /users/admin).
POST /sessions -> GET /reports/me: Session must be established to identify the citizen for retrieving their reports.
POST /users -> POST /users/confirm: Account must be registered before confirmation code can be applied.
GET /api/categories -> POST /reports: Report creation requires selecting a valid category from the available list.
GET /reports/pending -> PUT /reports/{id}/review: Review operation applies only to reports in pending status.
GET /reports/assigned -> PUT /reports/{id}/assign-external: External assignment requires the report to be in assigned status and owned by the requester.
GET /streets -> GET /streets/{name}/reports: Street-specific reports require a valid street name obtained from autocomplete.
POST /users/admin -> GET /users/roles: Role listing is only valid in the context of admin user creation or management.

risks: Ambiguity in role-based access control: some endpoints (e.g., /reports/assigned) imply role checks but do not specify exact roles in documentation.
Anonymous report creation bypasses user identity, potentially complicating accountability or notification flows.
Telegram webhook endpoint lacks authentication, risking unauthorized bot updates if secret tokens are not validated server-side.
Confirmation code expiration (30 minutes) is documented but not enforced via API response codes; client must handle timeouts.
External maintainer status updates (/reports/{id}/status) lack explicit validation of maintainer ownership in documentation.
